observation.visible_scene: Two crested, red-vented bulbul-like birds sit perched side by side on a thin wire that runs diagonally from lower-left to upper-right, set against a blurred grayish-brown tarp or wall. The left bird is slightly lower on the wire; both show black heads with crests, white cheek patches, pale breasts, dark wings, red undertail coverts and long white-tipped tails hanging downward.
visible_changes: The left bird repeatedly rotates its head and crest, swinging it between an up-left orientation and an up-right orientation (pointing toward its companion) several times across the clip; its body and feet stay fixed on the wire.

For most of the excerpt the right bird holds its head turned left, beak aimed at the companion, with a low, rounded crown; in the final frames (roughly the last fifth of the clip) it raises its black crest into a tall sharp point and turns its head/upper body so the white cheek patch and pale breast face more toward the camera.
Neither bird walks, hops, or flies along the wire; their perch positions and hanging tails remain essentially unchanged throughout.
The wire angle and background features stay fixed relative to the frame edges, so the visible motion is the birds' own head/body rotations rather than camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: What motivates the head turns or whether the two birds are interacting (courtship, threat, preening) is not determinable from these frames.
Behavior before t=0 and after t=2.667 s is outside the segment.
Whether any vocalization accompanies the crest-raising is unknown.
uncertain_details: The left bird's head swings could be looking vs. preening; the frames do not disambiguate.
Minor handheld jitter versus a true background shift cannot be fully separated, but no deliberate pan/zoom is evident.
